_note: What each answer means, shown after it's picked. One per option, in code order. Exceptions use {case}.
president_court_ruling: Presidents must obey court rulings against them, can appeal through the courts, and shouldn't attack the judges who ruled.
Presidents must obey court rulings against them while they appeal, but it's fine for them to criticize the judge in public.
A president can ignore a ruling from one court until a higher court agrees with it.
A president can ignore any court ruling the president believes is wrong.
exec_orders_scope: Without Congress, a president should only manage how the executive branch itself runs, not make new policy.
A president should make policy alone only in a real emergency; otherwise wait for Congress.
A president can make policy alone wherever existing laws leave room for judgment, but not beyond what those laws allow.
A president can make policy by executive order whenever the president decides it's needed, even if Congress has refused.
refuse_to_spend: When Congress funds a program, the president has to spend the money as directed, even on programs the president opposes.
The president can hold money briefly while asking Congress to cancel it, but has to spend it if Congress says no.
The president can decline to spend money Congress approved whenever the president thinks the program is wasteful.
refuse_to_spend_cases: The president must spend money Congress approved for this: {case}.
The president can refuse to spend money Congress approved for this: {case}.
emergency_duration: A president gets no emergency powers until Congress votes to approve them.
Emergency powers end after 30 days unless Congress votes to keep them.
Emergency powers end after 6 months unless Congress votes to keep them.
A president decides how long an emergency lasts, and it continues until the president ends it or Congress overrides a veto.
emergency_funding: Congress alone decides spending. A president can't use an emergency to pay for something Congress refused to fund.
A president can move money without Congress only for a sudden threat like an attack, and only until Congress can act.
A president can declare an emergency and fund a project Congress refused whenever the president judges the need is urgent.
emergency_funding_cases: A president should not be able to use an emergency to pay for this after Congress refused: {case}.
A president should be able to use an emergency to pay for this after Congress refused: {case}.
civil_service: Career government workers keep their jobs even when they disagree with the president's policies.
A president can fire senior officials who shape policy for disagreeing, but regular career staff stay protected.
A president should be able to fire most federal workers for any reason, including disagreeing with the president.
independent_agencies: More agencies should have leaders the president can't fire over policy, beyond the ones that already work this way.
The agencies that are independent today should stay that way, and no more should be added.
Only the Federal Reserve should be independent. A president should be able to fire the leaders of every other agency.
A president should be able to fire the leader of any agency, including the Federal Reserve.
prosecute_opponents: A president should have no say in whether the Justice Department investigates anyone, including the president's critics.
A president can tell the Justice Department about concerns, but career prosecutors decide whether to investigate.
A president can order the Justice Department to investigate specific people, including political opponents, whom the president believes broke the law.
pardon_allies: Presidents should be barred, by a constitutional amendment, from pardoning family, associates or political allies.
Presidents can legally pardon family and allies, but they should almost never use that power.
It's fine for a president to pardon family or allies whom the president believes were treated unfairly.
accept_results: Once courts and election officials confirm the result, the losing candidate should concede.
The losing candidate should accept the confirmed result, but it's fine to keep saying in public that it was stolen.
The losing candidate can keep fighting a confirmed result, including asking legislators to overturn it.
The losing candidate can refuse to accept a confirmed result and call on supporters to resist it.

s: I strongly prefer a system where no single leader can act without others agreeing, even if needed changes take years.
I somewhat prefer strong checks on leaders over speed.
I somewhat prefer letting elected leaders act quickly over strong checks.
I strongly prefer letting an elected leader act quickly, even with fewer checks on mistakes or abuse.
checks_vs_action.torn: I value checks on leaders and the ability to act quickly about equally.

s: Courts should strike down unconstitutional laws even when most voters support them, every time.
Courts should usually strike down unconstitutional laws, even popular ones.
When most voters clearly support a law, courts should usually let it stand.
When most voters clearly support a law, courts should almost never overrule it, even if it takes away some people's rights.
courts_vs_majority.torn: I'm torn between courts protecting rights and voters getting the laws they support.

filibuster: Bills should keep needing 60 votes, and judges and cabinet members should need 60 votes to be confirmed too.
The 60-vote rule for bills should stay exactly as it is.
Keep the 60-vote rule, but senators blocking a bill should have to hold the floor and keep speaking.
Some kinds of bills, such as voting rights or budget bills, should pass with a simple majority; the rest still need 60.
Every bill should pass the Senate with a simple majority of 51 votes.
filibuster_cases: This should still need 60 votes in the Senate: {case}.
A simple majority of 51 senators should be able to pass this: {case}.
rule_bending_leader: A president should never work around laws, court rulings or official procedures, even to deliver what voters chose.
A president can work around laws or procedures only in a real emergency.
A president can work around laws or procedures when they clearly block what voters chose.
The country needs a president who's willing to work around laws and procedures to deliver what voters chose.
political_violence: Violence to reach political goals is never justified in the US today.
Violence is justified only against a government that has taken power illegally.
Violence is sometimes justified when peaceful ways of changing things have failed.
court_expansion: Congress should add Supreme Court justices when the party in power wants different rulings.
The number of justices should change only as part of a reform both parties agree to.
The Supreme Court should stay at 9 justices.
presidential_immunity: Former presidents can be criminally prosecuted for what they did in office, like anyone else.
Former presidents are immune only for core duties the Constitution gives them, like vetoes and pardons; other acts can be prosecuted.
Former presidents can't be prosecuted for anything they did as part of their official job.
press_retaliation: A president should never punish news outlets over their coverage.
A president can limit an outlet's access to briefings and events, but can't go after its broadcast license.
A president can punish outlets the president believes spread falsehoods, including by pulling broadcast licenses.
agency_deference: When a law is unclear, courts should usually go with how the agency running it reads it.
Courts should go with the agency's reading of an unclear law only on technical or scientific questions.
Judges should decide what an unclear law means themselves, without deferring to the agency.
